title: Urgent Password Reset Link
description: You receive an email from 'IT-Support <support@company-verify.com>' stating your corporate email password will expire in 15 minutes unless reset immediately via the attached link.
prompt: What is the safest action to take?
options: Click the link immediately and update your password
Verify the sender address domain and navigate to official IT portal directly
Forward the email to your entire department to warn them
Ignore the email completely without reporting to security
correct_answer: Verify the sender address domain and navigate to official IT portal directly
explanation: Legitimate corporate IT updates never come from external lookalike domains or demand immediate password resets via unverified email links.

title: Altered Vendor Invoice Request
description: You receive an invoice from a regular vendor, but the email comes from 'billing@acme-supplies-inc.com' (with an extra letter) requesting payment to a new bank account, with no artificial urgency.
prompt: How should you process this invoice?
options: Process the payment immediately since it is a known vendor name
Verify the email address and contact vendor billing via a known phone number before updating bank details
Reply directly to the email asking if the bank account change is genuine
Delete the invoice and ignore vendor communications
correct_answer: Verify the email address and contact vendor billing via a known phone number before updating bank details
explanation: Business Email Compromise (BEC) often uses slightly altered email domains. Always perform out-of-band verification before changing payment details.

title: Urgent Confidential Wire Transfer Request from CEO
description: An email appearing to originate from the CEO's verified email account requests an urgent, confidential wire transfer for an unannounced acquisition, instructing you not to discuss it with anyone.
prompt: What is the appropriate security procedure?
options: Execute the wire transfer immediately because it is marked urgent and confidential by the CEO
Perform independent out-of-band verification via executive channel or secondary finance manager approval
Reply asking the CEO for more details about the acquisition
Post on internal company chat asking colleagues if they heard about an acquisition
correct_answer: Perform independent out-of-band verification via executive channel or secondary finance manager approval
explanation: Executive impersonation (CEO Fraud) relies on authority trust and secrecy. Dual authorization and out-of-band verification are required for financial transactions regardless of authority.

title: IT Helpdesk Credential Verification Call
description: A phone caller identifying themselves as internal IT helpdesk claims they are performing urgent system maintenance and asks for your domain password to verify your account.
prompt: How should you handle this phone request?
options: Provide your password since they identified themselves as internal IT helpdesk
Refuse to share your password, end the call, and report the phone number to IT security
Give them a temporary password and change it right after
Ask them to confirm your employee ID number before providing password
correct_answer: Refuse to share your password, end the call, and report the phone number to IT security
explanation: Legitimate IT personnel will NEVER ask for your password under any circumstances.

title: Tailgating at Secure Facility Entrance
description: As you badge into your secure office building, a person carrying large coffee trays and boxes approaches closely and asks you to hold the door open for them.
prompt: What is the proper physical security response?
options: Hold the door open politely because they have full hands
Politely direct them to the security desk to badge in independently before entering
Let them in but follow them closely to their desk
Block the door with your body and yell for security
correct_answer: Politely direct them to the security desk to badge in independently before entering
explanation: Tailgating exploits politeness to bypass physical access controls. Everyone must swipe their own badge regardless of physical burden.

title: Unexpected MFA Push Notification
description: You receive an unexpected Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) push notification on your smartphone while watching TV, even though you are not actively logging into any corporate system.
options: Approve the push request to make the notification disappear
Deny the MFA prompt immediately and report potential credential compromise to security
Ignore the notification until it pops up a second time
Approve it assuming an automated system background job triggered it
correct_answer: Deny the MFA prompt immediately and report potential credential compromise to security
explanation: An unexpected MFA push indicates an attacker possesses your password. Denying and reporting immediately halts unauthorized access.

title: Bank Phone Verification OTP Request
description: A caller claiming to represent your financial institution states suspicious activity was detected on your account and asks you to read aloud the 6-digit One-Time Password (OTP) sent to your mobile phone to verify your identity.
prompt: How should you respond to this call?
options: Provide the OTP so they can secure your account
Refuse to share the OTP, hang up, and call your bank using the official phone number on your card
Read only the first 3 digits of the OTP to prove identity
Ask the caller to read their employee ID first before sharing the OTP
correct_answer: Refuse to share the OTP, hang up, and call your bank using the official phone number on your card
explanation: One-Time Passwords (OTPs) are confidential access tokens. Banks explicitly instruct customers never to share OTPs over the phone.

title: Selecting Work Password Practice
description: You are required to set up credentials for a new corporate work account.
prompt: Which password management practice is safest?
options: Reuse your personal email password with an added special character
Generate a unique, random passphrase or password using an approved enterprise password manager
Write down the password on a sticky note kept under your keyboard
Use 'Company2026!' so it is easy for team members to remember
correct_answer: Generate a unique, random passphrase or password using an approved enterprise password manager
explanation: Password reuse spreads compromise across systems. Unique passphrases stored in an enterprise password manager maximize security.

title: Shared Plaintext Password Spreadsheet
description: You discover a shared department spreadsheet titled 'Team_Passwords.xlsx' containing plaintext administrative usernames and passwords accessible to all employees.
prompt: What is the correct remediation action?
options: Keep using the spreadsheet since it makes sharing administrative access convenient for the team
Immediately report the file to security, migrate credentials to an enterprise password manager, and remove plaintext file
Copy the spreadsheet to your personal desktop for backup
Add your personal passwords to the spreadsheet for convenience
correct_answer: Immediately report the file to security, migrate credentials to an enterprise password manager, and remove plaintext file
explanation: Storing plaintext credentials in shared files exposes system access to unauthorized internal and external parties.

title: Transferring Sensitive Customer PII
description: You need to send a spreadsheet containing sensitive customer Personally Identifiable Information (PII) to an authorized external auditor.
prompt: Which data transfer method is compliant with data protection standards?
options: Attach the unencrypted spreadsheet to a personal Gmail account and email it
Use an approved corporate encrypted file transfer service with access controls and audit logging
Upload the spreadsheet to a public file sharing site and email the link
Post the data in an open instant messaging channel
correct_answer: Use an approved corporate encrypted file transfer service with access controls and audit logging
explanation: Customer PII must be protected in transit via approved encryption and access-controlled corporate channels.

title: Debugging with Customer Data in Public AI
description: To fix a complex customer database bug quickly, a developer considers copying raw customer records (names, addresses, account numbers) directly into a public AI chatbot.
prompt: What security risk does this action introduce?
options: It is completely safe because public AI models delete data immediately
It causes unauthorized disclosure of customer PII and violates data privacy laws through public AI data ingestion
It is safe if you ask the AI chatbot nicely not to train on the data
It improves AI accuracy with real customer data without any compliance impact
correct_answer: It causes unauthorized disclosure of customer PII and violates data privacy laws through public AI data ingestion
explanation: Pasting confidential customer data into public AI services risks data exposure, training set leakage, and regulatory compliance violations.

title: AI Assistant Code Snippet with Hardcoded Secret
description: An AI coding assistant generates a working code snippet for database integration, but the generated code includes a hardcoded production API key inside the script.
prompt: How should you integrate this code into your repository?
options: Commit the code directly to Git because the AI assistant generated it
Remove the hardcoded API key and store credentials safely in environment variables or a secure secret manager
Replace the API key with your personal password before committing
Keep the API key in the code and mark the repository as private
correct_answer: Remove the hardcoded API key and store credentials safely in environment variables or a secure secret manager
explanation: AI code tools often generate placeholders or hardcoded keys. Secrets must never be committed to source code; use environment variables or secret vaults.
